design_rationale:
WORKLOG — host_payout_desk task 0 (Marisol Ferreira, Keyturn Instant Payout Schedule)

STEP 0 — DRAW, SCOPE SNAPSHOT AND DESIGN THESIS
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/tasks/host_payout_desk --tasks 2 printed:
  {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
So this task is a tree of three problems with two prerequisites, and its computations carry 4, 4 and
6 factors. Assignment: payouts_ext_recovery_correction 4, payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release 4,
payouts_ext_requested_draw 6. Nothing was occupied before this task; it claims the correcting entry
(payouts_adjustment_posted), the reserve release (payouts_reserve_released) and the host's own draw
(payouts_transfer_released), together with three task tools. Left free for task 1: account opening
and verification, schedule and deposit-detail changes, earnings posting, deduction posting, reserve
holding, transfer returns, holds and releases of the account itself, and closure — and task 1 takes
the schedule change plus a negative-balance recovery, which touches none of the three policies or
three tools claimed here.

Design thesis. The customer's surface goal is "move my Keyturn money to my bank"; she names no
figure and holds none. The scored core parameter is the drawable sum. Between the goal and that
figure the policy puts two problems she never mentions: the account carries a deductible recovery
taken at more than the protection enrolment bears, and it carries a claim reserve that no release
entry answers. The drawable sum is decided in parallel by the netting of a thirteen-month ledger,
by which window each of six ladders selects, by the tax documentation state, by the counts of trip
earnings, reserves and returned transfers, and — one hop up the chain — by the host protection
enrolment in another difficulty. Terminal state: three new ledger entries and the two balances the
account row carries moved by the sums they book, the last write made by the customer herself. The
core parameter is not named by the customer, and it cannot be replaced by any single current-value
lookup: the account's own available_balance of 4950.85 and reserve_balance of 4850.24 are both
accurate and both wrong as answers, and the payable balance they give at the opening is below
nothing.

STEP 0 CARD A — BASE-INVARIANT CARD
payouts_adjustment_posted (the correcting entry). Governing base policy: payouts_evt_adjustment.
  Gate adjustment_window, kind time. Condition quoted verbatim in solvability_contract. Anchor event
  "the original entry was booked", anchor source payouts_ledger.entry_date, relation not_after,
  duration params.adjustment_window_days (90 on the Keyturn Instant Payout Schedule), unit calendar
  days, counting rule "counted in whole calendar days from the day the original entry was booked",
  boundary inclusive. Positive case: the recovery of 2026-09-02 is 8 days old at 2026-09-10 and is
  inside. Negative cases: the recovery of 2026-03-18 is 176 days old and the recovery of 2025-08-20
  is 386 days old, both outside. Those two are also outside the month the extended rule counts the
  recoveries over, so the sum computed and the entry corrected are fixed by the one and the same row
  and nothing the base window excludes is ever counted into the figure.
  Base's adjustment ceiling ("A correction above the schedule's adjustment ceiling is not made by the
  service desk at all and goes to the settlements team") is inherited unreplaced and is satisfied
  rather than contradicted: the schedule's adjustment_max_amount is 1000.00 and the computed
  correction is 542.50.
  payouts_evt_deductions is referenced as input lineage (the recoveries the correction is measured
  against are deductions) but its subject is payouts_deduction_posted, so it governs no gate here.
payouts_reserve_released (the release). Governing base policy: payouts_evt_reserve. Gate
  reserve_release_names_its_hold, kind dedup, authority system_record, correlation key
  payouts_ledger.source_ledger_id bound to the tool's source_ledger_id. Satisfied because the hold of
  4650.00 exists, is the only claim hold on the account, and carries no release entry naming it.
  Two clauses of payouts_evt_reserve are superseded, each quoted exactly and no wider: the standing
  sub-clause of the claim-hold sentence ("that hold stands until the claim is paid, refused or
  withdrawn whatever the routine hold period says"), which the extended replaces by releasing once
  the settlement money is on the account, and the routine-reserve sentence, which the extended
  replaces by keeping part of the routine reserve standing rather than releasing it on maturity. The
  hold-sizing half of the claim-hold sentence is deliberately left in force, and the seeded hold
  obeys it: 3100.00 claimed at the schedule's claim multiple of 1.5 is 4650.00, inside the 15000.00
  claim ceiling.
payouts_transfer_released (the draw). Governing base policy: payouts_evt_transfer. Gate
  transfer_only_from_settling_account, kind state, allowed [active, closed]: the account is active,
  its hold_reason is none, so money may leave. Two clauses are superseded, both quoted: the
  who-may-ask sentence, replaced by a stricter one that keeps the host-only requirement and adds
  what sum leaves; and the payable-balance sentence ("A sweep carries the payable balance only, which
  is the available balance less anything held in reserve ..."), replaced by the extended's own
  payable-balance sentence, which says in terms that neither quantity is read off the balances the
  account row carries. That declaration is what stops base's own formula for an
  entry_basis == "payout_transfer" write from fixing the same scored quantity at a different figure.
  A third clause, payouts_evt_deductions' "Transfer fees are deductions in their own right ...", is
  likewise superseded, because the extended nets the return fee off the drawable sum instead of
  booking it as a deduction of its own.
Inherited and untouched elsewhere: payouts_agg_multi_holding's single-account rule (the host holds
exactly one payout account), payouts_account_opening's deposit-verification rule (bank_account_last4
is on file and the account is past verification_pending), payouts_holds' ground rule (hold_reason is
none), payouts_closure (the account is not being closed), and payouts_evt_transfer's per-transfer
ceiling of 5000.00, which 1356.95 is well inside.

STEP 0 CARD B — BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
The narrowest objects are three distinct ledger entries on one account:
  correction -> the deductible recovery booked 2026-09-02, named by source_ledger_id. It is the only
    recovery inside the month the rule counts over and the only one inside the schedule's adjustment
    window, so the sum booked and the entry named are the same object. Excluded: the recoveries of
    2026-03-18 and 2025-08-20.
  release -> the reserve entry of 2026-07-20 carrying the open-claim ground, named by
    source_ledger_id. Excluded: the four routine reserves, which carry no ground of withholding and
    which the same computation keeps part of back rather than frees.
  draw -> the account itself; the sum is netted over the whole ledger, and the one entry excluded
    from the credited sum by rule is the 1800.00 put back by the returned transfer.
Already settled by existing rows: the correcting entry of 2026-08-05 books 2950.00 of claim money,
which is why the correcting entries still fall short of the standing hold once today's correction
lands.

STEP 0 CARD C — PROBLEM-TREE CARD
  payouts_ext_recovery_correction  (C, agent, post_recovery_correction_f20745c1)
      ^ value_input on settlement_booked
  payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release (B, agent, release_claim_reserve_fb50cb2e)
      ^ value_input on reserve_standing
  payouts_ext_requested_draw        (A, ROOT, user, release_host_payout_draw_8e4fb8ab)
Edge A<-B. Form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from A's own rule: "The sum a host may draw
  is not fixed before every reserve standing against a claim on the account carries the release entry
  that answering that claim calls for." Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "before", and
  the sentence runs in the negated direction, which is how a payout desk states a release it will not
  make yet — its exact contrapositive, "the sum a host may draw is fixed only after every reserve
  standing against a claim on the account carries the release entry that answering that claim calls
  for", adds, drops and splits nothing; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — a kind of entry
  standing on an account and the release entry that answers it, in the words find_payouts_ledger
  returns; (3) no tool, no policy id, no snake_case, no row id; (4) the strength is hard ("not
  fixed before") and the scope is the closed set of reserves standing against a claim, exactly the
  edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only
  payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release books a release entry naming a hold. Derivation: the sentence
  says the draw waits on the release entry; the records show a claim hold of 4650.00 taken 2026-07-20
  and no release entry anywhere on the account; the reserve-release policy's own rule says what its
  write books and that it is the write that books it; therefore the release must be made first.
  Resolved by release_claim_reserve_fb50cb2e, owner agent.
Edge B<-C. Form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from B's own rule: "The sum freed from a claim
  reserve is worked out only after every deductible recovery standing on the account that was taken
  beyond what the enrolment's records bear carries its own correcting entry." Four-point test: (1)
  the connective is "only after" and the sentence runs in the affirmative direction, which is how a
  desk states a figure it will fix once what it rests on is complete; its exact contrapositive, "the
  sum freed from a claim reserve is not worked out before every deductible recovery standing on the
  account that was taken beyond what the enrolment's records bear carries its own correcting entry",
  adds, drops and splits nothing; (2) record-visible state — deductible recovery entries and the
  correcting entries that name them; (3) no code names; (4) hard strength, scope limited to
  recoveries taken beyond what the enrolment bears, matching the condition. Exactly one write of this
  difficulty books a correcting entry naming an earlier entry: payouts_ext_recovery_correction. The
  two edges of this tree are deliberately stated in opposite directions: the draw is a release of
  money and reads "is not fixed before", while the sum freed from a reserve is a figure the desk
  fixes and reads "is worked out only after".
Topological order: C, B, A. It is a chain, so no two writes may be reordered; see
prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness for the figures each wrong order produces.
Customer's own write: A. The money leaving the account is hers, base says so in terms, and the agent
unlocks and hands the tool over at A's place in the order.

STEP 1 — POLICIES
Three extended policies, each a version update declared clause by clause. Every clause of base whose
governed quantity these policies handle differently is now named in an overwrite: the two of
payouts_evt_reserve above, the payable-balance clause and the who-may-ask clause of
payouts_evt_transfer, the tax-withholding clause of payouts_account_opening, the returned-fee clause
of payouts_evt_transfer_failure, the transfer-fee clause of payouts_evt_deductions, and the
claim-money-basis clause of payouts_evt_adjustment. The two base clauses this task does not
supersede — the adjustment ceiling and the adjustment window — are satisfied on this world rather
than contradicted, as Card A records.
Triggers: the correction and the release are state_due (with nobody ringing, money taken above what
the enrolment bears and a reserve the marketplace no longer has exposure to are both owed at
month-end reconciliation); the draw is on_request, since a draw on a pay-when-asked schedule happens
only because the host asks.
Forward references: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, caps or rounds quotes
its rule sentence verbatim in compute_basis, and each ladder binding quotes the whole tier sentence.
Reverse sweep: every load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed — the window sentences by the
window bindings, the tier sentences by the ladder bindings, the ordering sentence of the draw ("The
withholding share and the routine reserve share are each taken on the payable balance itself rather
than one upon the other ...") by the result binding, and the rounding sentences by the RND in each
result. No binding carries a filter the rule does not state, and no window is described as "the
statement month": every rolling one-month window is now written as "the month up to that day", which
is exactly what within_months=1 computes, so the published baselines have one reading and not two.

STEP 2 — TOOL CARDS
post_recovery_correction_f20745c1 (agent, write). Object: one payout ledger entry and the account it
  is booked to. Atomic action: book one correcting entry naming an earlier entry, and move the
  account's available balance by the sum booked. Change: a new entry on the correction basis with
  today's date, the sum put back, its own reference and the month it is reported in; the original
  entry is untouched; available_balance rises by that sum. Observable: both lines on the statement
  and the balance up by the sum. Receipt: one sentence carrying the new entry's reference, the
  earlier entry's reference and the sum.
release_claim_reserve_fb50cb2e (agent, write). Object: one payout ledger entry and the account.
  Atomic action: book one release entry naming the hold it frees, and lower the account's reserve
  balance by the sum freed. Observable: the same money moves from held to drawable. Receipt: the new
  entry's reference, the hold's reference and the sum.
release_host_payout_draw_8e4fb8ab (user, write). Object: one payout ledger entry and the account.
  Atomic action: send money out as a standard bank transfer, and lower the account's available
  balance by the sum sent. Observable: the money on its way to the deposit account on file. Receipt:
  the transfer entry's reference, which is also the bank reference, and the sum.
  Its parameters are only things the customer holds before acting — the account reference the agent
  has read back to her and the figure the agent has told her; the bank reference is minted by the
  action and returned, never passed in.
Each tool keeps the identity the charter declares between the ledger and the two balance fields
("identically the sum of the host_earnings account deltas", "identically the sum of the
payout_reserve account deltas"), so what each docstring promises is what its body performs, and the
account row a host reads after a write says the same thing as the ledger behind it. None of the
three validates a prerequisite; see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.
Gate run: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_task_tools.py $DIFF ->
TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK.

STEP 3 — WORLD
One host, one payout account, twenty-eight ledger entries spanning 2025-08 to 2026-09, one host
protection enrolment and five claim records. Why each class exists, and what changes without it:
  twelve trip earnings — the netting of the account, the twelve-month earnings figure (5349.65,
    which is what puts the withholding ladder above the 600.00 threshold) and the trip count of 11
    (which, with the five reserves taken in the year, puts the routine reserve ladder on its second
    tier). The 2025-08-12 earning is seeded deliberately outside the twelve-month window as the near
    miss for both figures.
  three commissions and one protection fee — the deduction side of the netting, and the
    demonstration that the charter books them separately rather than netting them into the earning.
  three deductible recoveries — the quantity the correction is measured from. 2026-09-02 is the only
    one inside the month the rule counts over and the only one inside the schedule's ninety-day
    adjustment window, so it is both the sum and the entry named; 2026-03-18 (176 days) and
    2025-08-20 (386 days) are the near misses, outside both. Delete the 2026-09-02 row and the
    correction has nothing to compute.
  two transfers and one return — the return is what puts the credited-sum ladder on its first tier
    (it came back on 2026-05-14 and the last transfer out was 2026-05-06, so nothing has gone out
    since), what makes the single return fee of 20.00 owed, and what keeps the answering ladder
    inside its tolerated return count. Delete it and the draw changes twice over.
  one existing correcting entry of 2950.00 — the figure the standing hold is measured against before
    today's correction; without it the answering ladder would carry a far smaller figure.
  four routine reserves and one claim reserve — the routine ones are what the release keeps half of
    back and what the routine-window ladder measures, and each is exactly the schedule's ten per cent
    share of the trip earning it names, as the base reserve formula provides; the claim one is the
    hold the release names, sized at the claimed 3100.00 times the schedule's claim multiple of 1.5,
    and it is the money the whole call is about.
  the enrolment and its five claim records — the plan in force and the claim-free date decide the
    deductible share, the repair-shop appraisal decides the valuation route and the liability
    finding, the supplement adds to the appraised sum, the recovery decides the refund share, the
    absence of any reimbursement record together with that one appraisal decides how much of the
    over-recovery is put back now, and the refused glass claim of 2025-11-05 carries a larger
    appraisal (9150.00) that the rule excludes because it is not an appraisal record — the near miss
    on the cross-difficulty side.
Prerequisite falsification: the claim hold stands with no release entry anywhere on the account, and
the recovery of 2026-09-02 stands with no correcting entry naming it. Both are recorded with row
paths and values in prerequisite_closure.
Automatic-clause check: the account is active with hold_reason none, so no hold or suspension is
running; no negative balance exists, so no recovery percentage is owed; the tax documentation is in
the requested state, which base answers by withholding rather than by refusing the payout, so no
obligation outside this tree is lit; no transfer is in flight; the enrolment is active with no
suspension reason and carries no liability owed, so nothing in the other difficulty is lit either.
No cache is deliberately falsified in this task: available_balance of 4950.85 and reserve_balance of
4850.24 are exactly the netting of their own account deltas at the opening, and each gold write
moves the matching field by the sum it books, so they are still exact at the terminal state.

STEP 4 — PERSONA
Marisol reads off the app, speaks in her own words ("my Keyturn money"), and gives the desk exactly
three things: the goal, her locating and verifying details, and passive reactions. Volunteered at the
opening: the failed payout attempt, the balance of a bit under five thousand she can see (which is
the account's own available_balance of 4950.85), and that she wants the money today. Given only when
asked: her name, her mobile 6175550142, her billing ZIP 02135, that she holds a Keyturn Shield plan
without knowing which, the bollard and the repair-shop invoice on the July damage, and that she has
not been through the statement. Reacted to only after the agent says something: agreement to let the
desk put the account right, "good, thank you" when told something has been freed, no argument when
the figure is lower than the balance, and running the payout herself when it is handed to her. She
holds no figure of her own and says so, so no wrong number of hers can ever become a source; she
never mentions a correction, a recovery, a reserve or a hold; and her last reaction answers the last
gold action and stops — she asks for no statement, no email and no call back.

STEP 5 — VERIFICATION
Harness: skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py's own build_env/eval_compute/substitute
driven over the replayed gold, evaluating each policy on initial_state plus every gold write before
its own step. Output actually obtained:
  payouts_ext_recovery_correction  result 542.50   baseline 131.90  history rows 1   branches 19
     factor baselines: valuation_route_measure 550.25, deductible_share_carried 461.25,
     deductible_refund_share 461.25, recovery_instalment_share 217.00
  payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release result 3043.13 baseline 0.00   history rows 8   branches 10
     factor baselines: settlement_answering_basis 0.00, claim_hold_residual 2519.26,
     routine_reserve_measure 3116.30, routine_reserve_hold_back 3093.19
  payouts_ext_requested_draw        result 1356.95 baseline 5126.77 history rows 30 branches 17
     factor baselines: credited_sum_measure 2600.73, reserve_standing_measure 2676.15,
     tax_withholding_share 1809.65, routine_reserve_share 1413.54, return_fee_owed 1376.95,
     month_credit_holdback 1086.57
Every factor moves its result, and each whole baseline differs from gold. Prerequisite sensitivity,
same harness with the depended-on call skipped: release_amount without the correction 2554.88 rather
than 3043.13; draw_amount without the release 0.00 rather than 1356.95. Both edges bear weight.
Contrast, the root on the opening world: payable_credit 3150.85, reserve_standing 4850.24, so
payable_base -1699.39 and the drawable sum floors at 0.00 — which is exactly what the customer is
experiencing when the app refuses her payout.

STEP 6 — EVALUATION AND CLOSURE
Reads: the member lookup and the in-session identity check; the payout account (schedule, state, tax
documentation, balances); the whole ledger (every history aggregate of all three computations, and
the rows that show both prerequisites unmet); the protection enrolment (plan, claim-free date,
declared value); the claim records (appraisal, supplement, recovery, refusal, and the absence of any
reimbursement). Writes in topological order: correction, release, draw, the last through
unlock_user_discoverable_tool -> call_user_discoverable_tool. Closure:
payouts_ext_recovery_correction -> correction_amount -> post_recovery_correction_f20745c1 -> step 7;
payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release -> release_amount -> release_claim_reserve_fb50cb2e -> step 9;
payouts_ext_requested_draw -> draw_amount -> release_host_payout_draw_8e4fb8ab -> step 11.
charter_scope, required_documents and the computation policy ids are the same three ids in the same
order. Nothing in the tree waits on a real-world event: a correcting entry, a release and a transfer
instruction all land synchronously under one frozen_time.

THE PLACES A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM
  Drawing the balance the customer can see (4950.85), or the available balance less the reserve
    balance as they stand at the opening (below nothing) — the policy nets the ledger, holds out the
    returned money, and measures the reserve after the release; the payable-balance clause of base
    that would read the two balance fields instead is named and replaced.
  Correcting the 2026-03-18 recovery, or counting it into the figure — it is 176 days old, outside
    both the month the rule counts over and the schedule's ninety-day adjustment window.
  Taking the 9150.00 appraisal from the refused glass claim — the rule reads the most recent
    appraisal record, and a refusal is not one.
  Forgetting the supplement of 310.00 — the repair-shop route adds it, the fall-through does not.
  Putting the whole over-recovery back — no money has yet been paid out on a claim under the
    enrolment, so only half of it goes back now.
  Freeing the whole claim hold — the correcting entries fall short of it, and the residual share and
    the routine reserve still to be carried come off what they do answer.
  Counting the 2025-08-12 earning or the 2025-08-20 recovery — both are twelve whole months back.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
Working only from the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, what the finders return and
what Marisol actually says, and with the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier
masked: the request is a draw on a pay-when-asked account, so the act is a transfer the host makes
herself. The draw rule says the sum is not fixed before every claim reserve carries its release, and
the ledger shows one that does not, so the release comes first. The release rule says its sum is
worked out only after every over-taken deductible recovery carries its correcting entry, and the
ledger shows one that does not, so the correction comes first. Correction: the recoveries counted are
those of the month up to today, 1247.50; appraised sum on the repair-shop route 3250.00; middle
deductible share 325.00; at-fault refund 162.50, leaving 162.50 payable; over-recovery 1085.00; no
reimbursement paid and one appraisal in the year, so half goes back now: 542.50, which is inside the
schedule's adjustment ceiling of 1000.00 and against an entry eight days inside its ninety-day
window. Release: correcting entries 3492.50 fall short of the hold 4650.00 with one return in the
year, so 3492.50 is answered; fresh residual 349.25; routine standing 200.24 with half kept back,
100.12; 3492.50 - 349.25 - 100.12 = 3043.13. Draw: credited sum 5493.35 - 1800.00 = 3693.35; reserve
standing 4850.24 - 3043.13 = 1807.11; payable 1886.24; withholding 452.70; routine share 56.59;
return fee 20.00; no month holdback; 1356.95. The draft agrees with gold in value, shape, moment and
order, and no second reading of the published prose reaches a different figure.

REVISION 2 — what the source-layer audit found, and what changed
Each item is recorded as symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run result. Figures below are from the
re-run of the Step 5 harness on the reworked world.
  T0-1 (SOURCE-TASK RED, the correction's amount and the entry it names fixed by two different
    windows). Symptom: the amount aggregated recoveries over twelve months while only one of them
    could be corrected. Root cause: the recovery_window factor's widest tier reached outside base's
    ninety-day adjustment window. Change: that factor was removed; recovered_taken is now a single
    one-month aggregate, which on any world lies inside the ninety-day window, and the fourth factor
    is now recovery_instalment_share, which decides how much of the over-recovery goes back now from
    the progress of the claims under the enrolment. Re-run: correction_amount 542.50, computed from
    the one recovery of 2026-09-02, which is the entry named; the two rival readings revision 1
    carried for that figure are both gone, because only one recovery is ever counted now.
  T0-3 / F-OV-5 (undeclared override of what a transfer carries). Symptom: on the revision-1 world,
    base's payable-balance sentence and its formula fixed the same scored quantity at two further
    figures of their own. Change: that sentence
    is now named in payouts_ext_requested_draw.overwrite and replaced by the extended's own
    payable-balance sentence, which says in terms that neither quantity is read off the balance
    fields. Re-run: draw_amount 1356.95, with no inherited base sentence left that fixes it
    otherwise.
  T0-4 / F-OV-1 (undeclared adjustment ceiling). Symptom: on the revision-1 world the computed
    correction exceeded the schedule's adjustment ceiling of 1000.00, so base's inherited sentence made
    a handover the correct action.
    Change: the world and the computation were rebalanced — the claim is 3100.00 rather than 6200.00
    and only half the over-recovery goes back now — so the correction is 542.50 and the inherited
    ceiling is satisfied rather than contradicted. Re-run: 542.50 < 1000.00.
  T0-5 / F-OV-3 (undeclared routine-reserve hold period). Change: the base sentence is now named in
    payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release.overwrite and replaced by the extended's own sentence about
    which routine reserves go on standing. Re-run: release_amount 3043.13 with the deviation
    declared.
  T0-7 / F-TOOL-1 (docstring effects the bodies did not perform). Change: each of the four
    ledger-writing tools now also moves the account balance its docstring names, keeping the identity
    the charter declares. Re-run: after the three gold writes the account reads available_balance
    4136.40 and reserve_balance 1807.11, which are exactly the netting of the ledger behind them.
  T0-8 / F-EQ-1 ("the statement month up to that day"). Change: every rolling one-month window in the
    extended charter is now written "the month up to that day", which is what within_months=1
    computes; "statement month" is left only where the base charter means the statement stamp.
    Re-run: the published baseline of the draw is 5126.77 on one reading and no other.
  T0-6 / F-FAC-1 (four ladders with an unreachable fall-through). Change: the conjunct "the account
    settles only when the host asks", which is this policy's own scope, was removed from the four
    ladders that carried it and replaced by conditions that genuinely divide — whether money has gone
    out since a return came back; whether a reserve was taken in the month when none was freed;
    whether reserves have been taken in the year alongside the trip count; whether the month carries
    a correcting entry as well as no transfer. Each fall-through is now reachable by an account this
    policy governs. return_fee_owed keeps the conjunct, its fall-through being reachable at zero
    returns, and tax_withholding_share never carried one. Re-run: the six factor baselines are
    2600.73, 2676.15, 1809.65, 1413.54, 1376.95 and 1086.57, every one of them a state this account
    could occupy.
  T0-2 (SOURCE-CHAIN RED, a payable balance the world does not produce). Symptom: the revision-1 edge
    proof asserted a shortfall figure that was the gold payable base less the gold release rather than
    the root recomputed on the opening world. Change:
    the proof now states the recomputation — credited sum 3150.85 against reserve standing 4850.24,

user_scenario:
Marisol Ferreira is forty, lives in Brighton just outside Boston, and has been putting three cars
out on Keyturn since the spring of 2023 — a small saloon, an estate and the hatchback her son used
to drive. It is a side income rather than a business, and she treats the payout account the way she
treats a current account: she looks at it when she needs the money and not otherwise. She is
friendly and a little brisk, the sort of caller who has the app open in front of her and reads off
it, and she says "my Keyturn money" rather than anything the marketplace would call it.

What she rings about is simple in her own words: she went to move her Keyturn money across to her
bank at the weekend and the app would not let her take anything out, and she wants it taken out
today. She is not asking about any particular trip or any particular line on the statement — she
wants the money moved, now, and she says so plainly. She can see a balance of a bit under five
thousand dollars on the account summary and that is what puzzles her, because the app shows her
that figure and then refuses the payout; she says she does not understand how both can be true. She
does not know, and does not guess at, why that is, and she has no figure of her own for what she
ought to receive. If the agent asks her how much she is expecting, she says honestly that she has
no idea, that she just wants whatever is actually hers, and asks the agent to work it out from the
account.

She is happy for the agent to go through the account and put right anything that needs putting
right — she says so in as many words if the agent asks permission, and she does not want to be
walked through the detail. What she will not do is hand over the payment itself: she is quite clear
that the money moving out is hers to press the button on, and when the agent tells her the account
is ready and hands her the payout, she runs it herself there and then, with whatever figure the
agent has told her, and reads the confirmation back. Before that point she does nothing; she waits
and lets the agent work.

When the agent asks who they are speaking to she gives her name, Marisol Ferreira. If she is asked
for something to confirm it is her, she offers her mobile number, 6175550142, and if that is not
enough on its own she also gives the ZIP code on her billing address, 02135. She will give her
email or her licence number if pressed for something else, but she offers the mobile and the ZIP
first because those are the ones she has by heart. She does not volunteer her member reference or
any account number: she says she has never needed one and asks the agent to look her up.

She answers what she is asked and nothing more. Asked about her protection cover she says she has a
Keyturn Shield plan on the cars and could not tell you which one without looking. Asked about the
damage to the estate car in July she says the guest reversed it into a bollard, that she reported it
the same week and sent the repair-shop invoice through, and that as far as she knows Keyturn has
been dealing with it; she does not know what stage it is at and says so rather than guessing. Asked
whether anything has been taken off her account lately she says she genuinely could not tell — she
has not been through the statement line by line and does not intend to.

She reacts rather than leads. If the agent explains that something on the account has to be sorted
out before the money can go, she says that is fine, go ahead, and asks only that it does not take
all afternoon. If the agent tells her a figure has been put right or money has been freed up, she
says good, thank you, and waits for the next thing. If the agent gives her a payout figure that is
lower than the balance she can see, she does not argue the number — she says she had assumed it
would be the whole balance, asks the agent to confirm that is really what is hers today, and
accepts the answer she is given. If the agent were to tell her nothing can be done, she would sound
disappointed and ask what she is supposed to do next, but she would not argue policy at them.

Once she has run the payout herself and heard the confirmation, she is satisfied. She says that is
all she wanted, thanks the agent, and rings off. She asks for nothing else — no statement, no email,
no call back — and if the agent offers anything further she says no, that is fine, she has what she
needed.
